# Reading notes

- All pages were read on 2026-11-12 (13:40 to 14:00 MST). The documentation is at `docs.x.ai/grok-bot/*`; every page is also served as markdown at the same URL plus `.md`, which is what I read.
- The vendor names itself "SpaceXSI (xAI)" on these pages, and Grok Bot signs in with a Cursor account ("Grok Bot uses your Cursor account, so there's no separate login", https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/get-started). Admin controls live on the Cursor dashboard. I treated docs.x.ai, x.ai and the cursor.com pages the Grok Bot docs link to as the vendor's own material.
- Availability: "Grok Bot 1.0 is available starting today" (https://x.ai/news/grok-bot-1-0, Nov 2, 2026) and "Grok Bot is out of beta." (https://x.ai/bot). I write GA for features with no other label. Team Bots need a Team or Enterprise plan. "Enterprise only" is the vendor's own label and is repeated in the Availability column.
- Three kinds of agent appear in the pages: a personal Bot, a Team Bot (one Bot many teammates chat with), and a Cursor Cloud Agent that a Bot delegates coding work to. Values below rate the product as a whole and say when a feature is limited to one kind.

Count: yes 12, part 12 (7 DISPUTABLE toward yes; Directory is derived), no 1, not assessed 0.

# Four further questions

## 1. Areas of work (C1 to C4 of rerate-criteria-v2)

**C1. An area of work exists in the model: part, DISPUTABLE (yes).**
Quote for part: "Group Bots by project, client, or business with sections: right-click a Bot and choose **Move to new section**, or **Move to** once you have sections. Sections sync between desktop and iOS." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/bots#organize-your-roster). A section is a unit for an area of work that holds several Bots and can exist several times, but it has no definition or stated properties beyond the sidebar.
Reason yes is defensible: the product also has teams, groups and an organization, which are defined organizational units with stated properties, hold several Bots and roles, and exist side by side: "Share a Bot the way you'd share a doc: with your Cursor team, your whole organization, or only certain people and groups." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/team-bots) and "**Group Rules.** Rules for the group's Bots, combined with Team Rules." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/teams-and-enterprises#group-settings). I gave the lower value because the pages define a team or group as a set of members for access and policy ("To widen that baseline for one cohort"), and a personal Bot belongs to a user, not to a team; the pages do not say a team or group divides the system's work into areas.

**C2. The area is specified apart from who does the work: part.**
Rated on the team and group (the only defined unit). Unit-level properties are rules and roles: "Rules that every member's Bots follow. Add them from the Grok Bot page and scope each rule to Cursor, Grok Bot, or both." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/teams-and-enterprises#team-rules), with roles defined apart from who fills them (team admin, member; on a Team Bot, owner, "**Manager**" and "**Collaborator**", https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/team-bots#how-do-i-share-a-bot-with-my-team). No page states what a team, group or section as a whole is responsible for. Responsibility is stated per agent: "In your first message, give the Bot its job, sources, and approval boundaries, and ask it to remember them." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/bots#create-a-bot).

**C3. A record of accountability: part.**
"Lists every Bot on your team. Open **Manage Bots** under **Shared Bots** on the Grok Bot page, and filter the list by sharing or by owner." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/teams-and-enterprises#manage-bots); also "The list shows Bots shared with you, and each one shows who made it." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/team-bots#how-do-teammates-find-a-team-bot). The record names one owner per agent, not one accountable area or owner per responsibility or capability. Searched the docs for "accountab", "responsib", "owner": no record keyed by responsibility. (A marketplace template, Alfred, instructs a Bot to keep a "Bot Registry" with "clear human owners"; it is a user-authored template, not a product record, and I did not count it.)

**C4. Finding where to send work: part, DISPUTABLE (yes).**
"Ask one of your Bots in your own chat, for example 'Is there a Team Bot for on-call triage?' It searches the Team Bots you can use by what they do, and tells you which ones you've already added." (the source uses double quotation marks around the example question) (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/team-bots#how-do-teammates-find-a-team-bot). Changelog: "A Team Bot can suggest other team Bots that fit a request and link to a chat with one." (https://x.ai/changelog/bot, v0.78.4) and "In a DM with a Team Bot, teammates can have it message other Team Bots they can use." (v0.77.0).
Reason yes is defensible: a Bot looks up, from a kind of work, the Team Bot that handles it and returns a way to reach it. I gave the lower value because the lookup covers only Team Bots shared with the asking person (Team and Enterprise plans), the pages describe it as answering a person and do not say a Bot uses it to route its own work, and for personal Bots routing is inside one orchestrator: "It checks in with you on its own and coordinates your other Bots. You could send the conference request to your primary Bot, and it could pass the work to your expenses Bot." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/how-grok-bot-works#your-primary-bot-and-bots-with-one-job).

**Directory (derived): part** (C3 part, C4 part; it would stay part if C4 were yes).

## 2. Supplied agents for an area of work

Yes, as templates in a marketplace that is sorted by area of work. The categories on https://x.ai/bot/marketplace are "From Grok Bot Team Engineering Sales Marketing Design Personal Recruiting & People Product Operations". Authorship caveat from the docs: "Shared templates are created by other users, not by Grok Bot." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/bots#share-a-bot); each template carries an author's name, including those on the "From Grok Bot Team" shelf.

- Shelf "From Grok Bot Team" (https://x.ai/bot/marketplace): "Outbound Prospecting by Krista Letz Finds prospects that match your ideal customer, then drafts a first message to each one."; "SEO & AEO Desk by Adam Tanguay Turns your keywords into content ideas and writer-ready briefs for search and AI answers."; "Haggle Bot by Daniel Gartshein Inventories your SaaS spend from Ramp and bills, finds evidence-backed savings"; "Recruiting Coordinator by Tommy Hansen Schedules interview loops, preps your interviewers, and chases what's stalled."
- Named in the documentation as "Prebuilt bots to get started" (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/overview): "Overheard", "Tradbot" ("Watches your personal email and calendar so school forms, bills, and RSVPs don't slip."), "Meeting Recap Deck", "Pitch Deck Coach".
- Builders named in the documentation (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/how-grok-bot-works): "dr eggbot — Asks you a few questions, then sets up the Bots for you, one job each." and "tinkabot — Wraps an API in a plugin made of an MCP server and skills, tests it, and publishes it only when you say so."
- Other marketplace entries by area (same page), for example Sales: "Sales Call Coach", "GTM Loop Closer"; Engineering: "QA bot", "Lingxi's Engineer Bot"; Operations: "Office Ops Desk", "Executive Assistant", "Alfred" ("Designs, audits, and governs your Grok Bot organization so it matches real company outcomes, with clear human owners and no duplicate jobs."); Recruiting & People: "Talent Discovery"; Product: "PM bot".
- Templates named in the changelog (https://x.ai/changelog/bot): "Order Concierge and Deal Watcher templates track your orders, refunds, and returns" (v0.77.0); "The Find unused subscriptions template cancels plans you pick" (v0.78.1).
- Not shipped agents, but vendor-written team set-ups by area that the primary Bot creates on request (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/use-cases#build-a-team-of-bots-for-a-bigger-goal): "Campaign team", "Month-end close", "Support queue" ("Ask your primary Bot to set up this team."). Guides by area (Marketing, Sales, Recruiting, Legal, Engineering, Support) are listed at https://x.ai/bot/guides.

## 3. What fits nowhere

- **Paying for things.** A payment instrument, order records and order tracking held by the product: "A card saved in Vault fills in at checkout without asking you each time, and no setting requires your approval for each use." and "A Bot can also send one order card for a batch of up to 500 card payments, paid with a saved card." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/vault#pay-for-things); "Orders placed through a connected store are tracked until they arrive." (https://x.ai/changelog/bot, v0.79.3). Secrets and Approvals cover the card and the consent; no service covers holding and spending money.
- **Usage metering and spend limits.** "**Grok Bot usage** charts your Grok Bot usage, **By Bot** or **By source**." and "**On-demand monthly limit**" (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/settings-and-notifications#usage-and-billing); "To control unattended usage, Grok Bot may ask whether to keep routines running after a long period away and pause them if there is no response." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/skills-routines-and-automations#routines-and-usage). Scheduling covers how much may run at once, not what work costs or a budget.
- **Unprompted initiative.** "Your primary Bot spots tasks it can handle for you and offers to do them." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/initiative). Deciding what work to propose is not Scheduling (when work starts) and not Orchestration (assigning known work). Borderline.
- **A person taking over the agent's environment.** "Open the computer, take control, complete only the blocked step, and tell the Bot to continue." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/computer-and-apps#take-over-for-a-sensitive-step). Shared live control of an Environment by a person is not an approval and not a channel message. Borderline (could be read as part of Environments).
- **Learning a procedure from a recorded demonstration.** "Teaching records visible computer interaction for up to ten minutes. [...] The learned skill is a draft." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/skills-routines-and-automations#teach-a-workflow-by-demonstration). Closest services are Improvement and Registry; the capture of a person's demonstration is covered by neither. Borderline. "Teach-by-demonstration may be enabled gradually."
- **Classifying what work agents do, for managers.** "Cursor classifies each Grok Bot conversation so admins can see what kind of work Bots handle across the team, without reading the conversations themselves." (https://cursor.com/docs/account/teams/analytics, Enterprise). Could be read as Observability; it reports kinds of work and "Level of Automation", not evidence of actions.

## 4. Where it runs and what the user supplies

- **Where:** the vendor's cloud. "Grok Bot runs only on Cursor-hosted cloud computers. On-premises deployment, deployment inside your own perimeter, and bring-your-own-image deployment are not supported today." and "Grok Bot computers run in the United States." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/security#hosting, #data-residency). "The desktop and mobile apps are thin clients for chat, review, and approvals." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/teams-and-enterprises#how-grok-bot-is-built). Optional reach into the user's machine: "Bots can act on a member's own machine through the desktop app: run commands, read files, and move files between the cloud computer and the local machine." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/security#local-execution), default "**Ask every time**".
- **Running while the user is away:** "Yes. Bot work runs on the cloud computer. Closing the app, laptop, or phone does not stop a background turn or routine." (https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/faq#does-grok-bot-keep-working-when-my-laptop-is-closed). Limits stated: approvals raised by background work expire "after 30 minutes"; routines may be paused "after a long period away"; work stops when weekly usage runs out unless on-demand usage is on.
- **What the user supplies:** a paid plan ("Premium, Super, and Ultra on The X Subscription include Grok Bot", https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/get-started); sign-ins to apps and websites ("A Bot has no access by default and acts only with accounts the member signs it into"); each Bot's job, rules and limits in chat ("Give each Bot one job in its first message and ask it to remember how you want the work done."); skills and routines for repeated work ("Start with a one-time task. Make it reliable, save the method as a skill, and only then automate it."); approval rules ("Add specific **Ask first** rules for sending, publishing, and deleting."); and the division of work among Bots ("In a group chat, make one Bot responsible for each step."). The user hosts nothing and builds no runtime. For an organization: the team's rules, connector policy, network policy and identity-provider setup, most of them Enterprise only.
